fields.title: Choreography instead of calls
fields.keyTakeaway: Events make adding reactions cheap at the price of the scenario no longer being readable in one place, which is compensated for by a correlation ID and a live event registry.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: Placing an order no longer "calls" a store notification — it publishes an event. What does this change for the product besides response speed?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: [[event-driven-architecture|Event-driven architecture]] makes adding new reactions almost free while making it almost impossible to answer the question "what happens after an order is placed." A PM who doesn't understand this tradeoff rejoices at the speed of the first features and doesn't understand why a year later no one can describe the full scenario.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Two ways to connect process steps.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **[[orchestration|Orchestration]].** There is a conductor component that knows the entire sequence: create order, charge money, notify store, accrue bonuses. The scenario is read in one place. Adding a step means editing the conductor.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **[[choreography|Choreography]].** A component publishes an event, and the rest decide for themselves whether to react. No one knows the whole picture. Adding a reaction touches no one.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: *Pros.* A new feature plugs in without modifying existing ones. Teams work independently. One subscriber failing does not break the others.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: *Cons.* The entire scenario is not written down anywhere. Understanding what happens after an action requires gathering all subscribers. A year later, this knowledge lives in the heads of one or two people.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: *Cons.* Debugging gets harder: the chain is distributed, and "why didn't the SMS arrive" turns into an investigation.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: Hence the mandatory tools without which choreography becomes unmanageable:
fields.sections/2/blocks/8/text: **[[correlation-id|Correlation ID]].** An operation tag travels through all events. It reconstructs the entire chain from the user action to the final consequence. Without it, [[traceability|traceability]] is impossible, and support cannot answer a client's question.
fields.sections/2/blocks/9/text: **Event registry.** A live list: what events exist, what they mean, who is subscribed. A document that must be maintained — otherwise in a year no one knows what breaks when things change.
fields.sections/2/blocks/10/text: Mature product practice is mixed: critical financial scenarios are explicitly orchestrated, side effects go via events.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Order placement: orchestration until payment confirmation (create → check stock → charge → confirm), then the `order.created` event and seven subscribers.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: The boundary is chosen by the criterion: **everything without which an order is not considered placed is orchestration; everything else is events.** This is also the transaction boundary from `DS1-N5` and the synchronicity boundary from `IN1-N4`, and the coincidence is not accidental.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: The correlation ID was introduced after an incident where a buyer received neither SMS nor push, but bonuses were credited. The investigation took two days: we had to manually match logs across four services. Now support enters the order number and sees the entire chain with timestamps — investigation takes minutes.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: The event registry appeared when changing the `order.created` structure revealed there were nine subscribers instead of seven: two were added by neighboring teams without telling anyone.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Events are not suitable where an immediate result is needed. Availability checks cannot be an event — the caller needs an answer now.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Events make adding reactions cheap at the price of the scenario no longer being readable in one place, which is compensated for by a correlation ID and a live event registry.
